exercise.name: Lying Leg Hip Raise
aliases: Flat bench leg raise with hip lift
Bench leg raise to hip thrust up

reference.title: Lying leg hip raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip flexion, then posterior pelvic tilt and lumbar flexion with the legs vertical)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the legs rise to vertical, breathe out as the hips curl off the mat, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s legs up, 1.1 s hips up, short pause, 1.7 s hips down, 1.9 s legs down

prescription.tempo: Legs up in about 1.5 s, hips up in 1 s, lower each part in about 2 s; no swinging
prescription.progression: Slower lowering and a longer pause with the hips up, then hanging leg hip raises.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench with the glutes near the end, grip the sides of the pad beside your head, legs straight out in line with the bench.
Keep the knees straight and lift the legs to vertical without arching the low back.
Breathe out and curl the hips up off the bench, driving the feet straight up toward the ceiling.
Roll the pelvis down onto the bench, then lower the legs slowly to level.
Keep the low back on the pad and the legs out straight before the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the legs to throw the hips up
mistakes.fix: Stop at vertical for a beat and lift the hips with the abdominals, not momentum.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the legs drop below the bench
mistakes.fix: Stop the legs level with the bench and keep the low back on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling hard on the bench with the arms
mistakes.fix: The grip only anchors you; keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the knees to make it easier
mistakes.fix: Keep the legs straight, or switch to the bent-knee hip raise.

kinematics.norm: From about level to vertical before the hips lift (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees with the legs vertical; straight-leg raises load the hip flexors heavily (Andersson 1997)
The pelvis curls until the buttocks clear the bench; this curl brings in the lower abdominals (Clark 2003)
Hands hold the bench behind or beside the head to anchor the upper body (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1-2 s per part (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5283, Lying leg hip raise, video (movement reference)

Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)
Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Straight-leg raising loads the hip flexors and the lumbar spine; low-back loads were among the higher of the abdominal exercises compared by Axler and McGill (1997).
Low-back pain or flexion intolerance: start with the dead bug or a bent-knee reverse crunch.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before straight-leg or trunk-flexion work.
modify: Hamstring tightness: allow a small knee bend.
Low back lifting at the start: begin with the legs a little above level.
regressions: Lying leg hip raise on the floor.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the pelvis toward the ribs to lift the hips; leg-raise variants with a pelvic curl raised lower rectus activity (Clark 2003).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris lift the straight legs to vertical (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris lift the straight legs to vertical (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help curl the pelvis and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help curl the pelvis and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull against the bench grip to keep the upper back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull against the bench grip to keep the upper back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bench to anchor the upper body (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bench to anchor the upper body (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Legs to vertical, then feet up
